== Biography ==
This Philip Glasco account carries an estimated 1740 birth and an existing tree father Philip Glasco-146. The profile quotes a younger designation in its 1772 inventory citation; the underlying entry was not independently rechecked here. Neither the estimated birth nor an explicit father clause is newly established. He remains a strong same-person match to the younger Dublin watchmaker Glasgow-3932, associated with Teresa Plunkett in 1768 and a reported death in 1770. A 1772 grant would not itself exclude a 1770 death, but the exact inventory identity and role still need verification. No merge, new spouse, parental confidence upgrade or exact vital date is established here.

=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

The [[Glasco-146]] parent profile is used provisionally for the elder watchmaker and is now selected under Thomas-1242, uncertain. This younger inventory-based account remains a strong same-person match to [[Glasgow-3932]], not a proved second younger Philip. The 1772 citation has not established its asserted 1740 birth, exact grant role or literal sonship. Existing father and mother fields remain unupgraded. The Dublin records name no Scottish parents, birthplace or apprenticeship, so the Scottish child and elder watchmaker may be different men. The fresh [[Glasco-146]] biography itself mixes the 1752 watchmaker with junior notices of 1765,1768 and 1770. Its c.1715 birth and the c.1740 birth of [[Glasco-147]] are tree estimates, not evidence selecting a generation. If [[Glasco-146]] instead represents the junior, the elder Philip is an alternative father-generation placement and the Thomas link would need revision; no competing father is attached alongside it. The elder placement is a preferred working interpretation of the profile’s trade/address and family structure, not a claim that every event in that biography belongs to him. The junior’s 1765 unnamed-wife death,1768 Teresa Plunkett marriage and reported 1770 death remain with the younger documentary account [[Glasgow-3932]]. [[Glasco-147]] is a strongly supported duplicate account of that younger man, but its quoted 1772 younger/inventory wording was not independently rechecked here and establishes neither the estimated birth nor a newly verified father clause; a grant date is not a death date. No merge, spouse transfer or new child attachment follows. Catherine Mangan is called [[Glasco-146]]’s mother in its prose but spouse in its structured family; the 1750 report describes the elder’s bride only as the widow Mangan, and the 1760 report gives no forename. Neither record proves maternity. Preserve the existing Mangan/Braccan and younger-parent fields as qualified leads; do not add a mother for [[Glasco-146]]. The father Thomas is common to the retained 1711 child records, while the 3 June Uphall versus 21 October Linlithgow Philip entries and their maternal readings remain unreconciled; Jean Duncan is not transferred as [[Glasco-146]]’s mother. The 1777 probate/court occurrence does not establish survival after 1772. The local elder account uses 1772 as an uncertain death year through the selected identity, retaining the old after 1772 value and all junior events in the comparison.

The current public API capture retains Teresa Plunkett as this profile’s spouse. Together with the unusual name, younger designation, trade and address in the previously inspected notices, this supports the existing strong match to [[Glasgow-3932]]; no live merge is performed.
